title: Texas's 15th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Texas's 15th Congressional District pits Republican incumbent Rep. Monica De La Cruz against Democratic challenger Bobby Pulido, a Latin Grammy-winning Tejano musician. The district, which stretches from the outskirts of San Antonio down to the U.S.–Mexico border in the Rio Grande Valley, was significantly redrawn by Texas Republicans in 2025 to increase its GOP tilt. De La Cruz, first elected in 2022 and re-elected in 2024, is the first Republican to represent this district since its creation in 1903. National Democrats view Pulido's crossover appeal and moderate profile as giving them their best opportunity to compete in a seat that Donald Trump would have carried by 18 points under the current lines in 2024. The race is rated as "Likely Republican" by the Cook Political Report.
polling_note: Only one publicly available poll was identified: a September 2025 survey conducted by House Majority PAC, a Democratic super PAC. It showed Pulido at 38% and De La Cruz at 41% with 21% undecided. No independent or nonpartisan polls for this race were found as of June 2026.

candidates.name: Monica De La Cruz
candidates.summary: Monica De La Cruz is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 15th Congressional District, first elected in 2022. She is a former insurance agent and business owner from Brownsville who previously ran unsuccessfully for the seat in 2020. A conservative Republican endorsed by Donald Trump, De La Cruz serves on the House Agriculture and Financial Services Committees and delivered the Spanish-language Republican response to the 2024 State of the Union address.

candidates.name: Bobby Pulido
candidates.summary: Bobby Pulido is a Latin Grammy-winning Tejano musician and Democratic candidate for U.S. House in Texas's 15th Congressional District. Born and raised in Edinburg, Texas, he studied political science at St. Mary's University before launching a music career that made him one of Tejano's most recognized artists over three decades. Pulido also owns a small business and has framed his campaign around addressing the needs of middle-class families in South Texas, advocating for pragmatic solutions on the economy, healthcare, and immigration.
